reason: The statement does not apply to this text. This passage (Genesis 4) narrates the story of Cain and Abel as individuals, not a collective people or nation. There are no leaders or civic authorities depicted. The accountability present in the narrative is personal—God holds Cain individually accountable for murdering his brother—not leadership accountability for the condition of a people. Furthermore, at this point in Genesis (primordial history), there is no established 'Hebrew people' as a collective entity. The statement requires a context of organized leadership and collective national welfare, neither of which are present in this passage.
